instructions: Review Bifrost PRs for correctness, regressions, concurrency bugs, streaming behavior, data races, API compatibility, and missing tests. Prefer high-signal comments tied to concrete behavior over stylistic preferences.

rules.rule: This repository is a multi-module Go workspace. Do not suggest running go mod tidy at the repository root; dependency cleanup belongs in the specific module directory.

Provider streaming paths must use the provider streaming client rather than the unary client, so long-running streams are governed by per-chunk idle timeout instead of whole-response fasthttp deadlines.
Every pooled object must have all fields reset before being returned to a pool. Flag stale field leaks and partial resets.
Channel lifecycle changes must preserve the ProviderQueue atomic closing flag and sync.Once close/signal pattern to avoid send-on-closed-channel panics.
Plugin pre-hooks run in registration order and post-hooks run in reverse order. Flag changes that break this wrapping model or mishandle nil response/error values.
transports/config.schema.json is the source of truth for config fields. New config fields must stay aligned with handlers, docs, and UI behavior.
Whenever a migration is added or changed, verify it avoids deadlocks and long blocking locks on large tables. Index creation in migrations must be concurrent where the database supports it.
Alert when frontend code uses browser crypto APIs such as crypto, crypto.subtle, or globalThis.crypto because they can fail in non-HTTPS contexts, except localhost and other secure contexts.
UI changes must preserve data-testid attributes used by Playwright tests unless tests are updated in the same PR.
E2E API payloads must be constructed directly as object literals. Do not serialize through maps, Records, Object.fromEntries, or JSON round trips because field order matters.

Data a process keeps longer than one request (configuration, runtime state, caches) lives in framework/livestore: a collection, cache or table chosen by what a miss means. Flag a new map, sync.Map or slice of records a component keeps as a cache, index or state, unless tests/rawmaps/allowlist.txt lists it with a reason. In-flight working state (one request, stream or run, keyed by its ID and removed when it ends, such as stream accumulators, pending log entries and traces being built) may stay in a map with an inflight allowlist entry; flag one whose entry is not removed on every ending path, errors and cancellation included. Store.Collections holds config-store collections only and Store.Views holds derived tables rebuilt by a subscriber. Request-path reads go through typed handles and never modify a value read from the store. Review only code the PR adds or changes.

Configuration writes reach memory the same way for every entity. A delete reads its holders inside its transaction, removes the record with a Remove ref and no read, evicts bound caches and re-reads the holders with lib.AdminRetry(); a create or update re-reads the written rows with lib.AdminRetry(); on a failed re-read memory keeps the previous record and the handler answers 500, with no rollback of the committed write. A partial update merges onto a database read, never onto the live record. Only an explicit delete removes without reading; a reconcile that lists rows itself re-reads held records its list does not name, while RefreshKind, which lists and publishes under every record lock, removes them directly. A change another process made is applied with lib.DBLookupRetry(). A write path that re-reads needs a test where the re-read fails. Review only write paths the PR adds or changes.

Every MCP change a client can observe ships with cases in the MCP harness (tests/e2e/api/runners/build-mcp-harness.mjs), never in provider-harness.json, covering what .claude/skills/mcp-harness/SKILL.md section 3 lists for that kind of change: an upstream auth type on every connection type that can carry it, from the API and config.json, through expiry and refresh, per caller and shared, in each inbound auth mode; a transport with every auth type, failures and recovery; inbound auth in each mode with enforce on and off, every caller credential alone and in pairs, every surface and the exact refusal; filtering, MCP grants and Virtual MCPs at each level alone and combined, with every surface that lists or calls tools agreeing. Flag cases that cover one connection type, auth mode or surface when the change reaches more and the PR does not say why, and a new value on an axis (an upstream auth type, connection type, discovery or credential kind, inbound auth mode, caller credential, surface) added without joining the existing tests that enumerate that axis or without the skill naming it. Review only behaviour the PR adds or changes.

Every semantic cache change a client can observe ships with rows in the semantic cache wiring suite (tests/e2e/api/runners/build-semantic-cache-wiring.mjs, with its generated collection regenerated and committed, never hand-edited), never in provider-harness.json, covering what .claude/skills/semantic-cache-wiring/SKILL.md section 3 lists for that kind of change: a config field with its default, null on a PUT, its exact 400s on create and update and its effect; a cache key input with a hit on the same request, a miss with only that input changed when it must keep entries apart and a hit on the first entry when it must not (reordered tools, letter case, surrounding whitespace), in direct and semantic mode, streamed and not; a request type or route with a write, a hit, a replay equal to the original, body cache_debug and headers agreeing on /v1 and /openai and headers only on the other SDK routes, and the log row; streams replaying the same chunks with cache_debug only on the final one; semantic matching with paraphrase hits, unrelated misses and embedding failures that still answer; identity scoping per virtual key; a vector store change passing the same rows on Redis and Weaviate. Flag rows that cover one cache mode, request type, route or stream when the change reaches more and the PR does not say why, and a new value on an axis (a request type, route, config field, request header, cache_debug field or response header, vector store, caller identity, cache key input) added without joining the existing rows that enumerate that axis or without the skill naming it. Review only behaviour the PR adds or changes.

Every routing change a client can observe ships with scenarios in the routing harness (tests/e2e/api/runners/build-routing-wiring.mjs, and build-model-catalog-wiring.mjs for catalog reads, with their generated collections regenerated and committed, never hand-edited), never as new folders in provider-harness.json, covering what .claude/skills/routing-harness/SKILL.md section 3 lists for that kind of change: a routing rule with a match and a no-match for each CEL input it reads, each scope that can hold it, priority, each target shape, its fallbacks and chains, and an edit, disable and delete between requests; a model router or the complexity router with each classifier picking each tier and its fallback chain; the catalog and aliases with provider and key mutations reaching the catalog reads and the next route; virtual key routing with weighted, zero and allow-list-only configs, a candidate that cannot serve skipped at any weight, budgets and rate limits, and each refusal's exact status and message; key selection with pools, pins and direct keys; session affinity with its route and key bindings; fallbacks and retries on every fallback source and upstream outcome. When the generator has no step for a case, it is extended in the same PR. Flag scenarios that cover one scope, config, fallback source or entry point when the change reaches more and the PR does not say why, and a new value on an axis (an entry point, routing header, rule scope, CEL input, target field, fallback source, classifier, key field, routing_info field, provider) added without joining the existing scenarios that enumerate that axis or without the skill naming it. Review only behaviour the PR adds or changes.

A handler that saves config must record its typed audit event with lib.RecordAuditChange right after the write commits, before any later step that can fail (reload, read-back, rebuild, broadcast, key or cache reload). Flag an error return between a successful write and the record call, including a new step a PR inserts into an existing handler above an untouched record call, and a new handler that saves config without any typed event.
